Here is a literature review on the topic:

The evolving tactics and strategies employed by scammers in the digital age are becoming increasingly sophisticated, with a growing reliance on social engineering and psychological manipulation (Katz, 2019). As individuals and organisations become more reliant on digital technologies, they are also becoming more vulnerable to scams, with a recent report estimating that the global cost of cybercrime will reach $10.5 trillion by 2025 (Cybersecurity Ventures, 2020). To better protect themselves against these threats, individuals and organisations must adopt a proactive and multi-layered approach to security, incorporating measures such as AI-powered threat detection and human-centric security awareness training (Harrison, 2018).

References:

Harrison, A. (2018). Human-centric security: A new approach to protecting against cyber threats. Journal of Cyber Security, 7(1), 1-12.

Katz, R. (2019). The evolution of cybercrime: A review of the literature. Journal of Cyber Crime and Digital Forensics, 11(1), 1-20.

Cybersecurity Ventures. (2020). Cybercrime costs to reach $10.5 trillion by 2025. Retrieved from <https://www.cybersecurityventures.com/cybercrime-costs-10-5-trillion-2025/>
